doc.title: Tom Albert and Milton "Mooney" Martin Interview, 1964-12-21

title: Economy Hall, Hope Hall and bandstands in the old halls
summary: They compare the balcony and bandstand in other old halls and the church Economy Hall. Hope Hall, whose front blew in during a hurricane, is due to be torn down, and they describe its high rear bandstand.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: I ain't been there before. Yeah. The other stand is still there. The choir sits up in there. Yeah. They have room for the choir. And I remember the artesian hall had a balcony up there. Yeah. All them halls had it.
All them halls. I guess Hope's Hall was the same way too. The cooperatives.
They're going to tear it down. It's the Hope's Hall they say. Did they tear it down?
They're going to. The front of it blew in that hurricane last. Oh that's right here at the church. Yeah. Yeah.
Oh yes. I see what. Mount Zion church is on. Yeah. I see what it was. A total big piece in the front of it. Yeah.
The whole front of it. They got built that on Robeson. They're going to tear it down eh? Yeah.
They got plenty of lumber there.
Yeah. A lot of good lumber in there I bet. Well I used to play in there too. I used to build there. Oh yeah. Where was the bandstand? In the front by the door? In the back. In the back. In the back.
Right in the back. You go up the stairs. You went to go the stairs go right there and you. And go all the way back to the bandstand.
Right in the back. Yeah. You go all the way back and in the back they had the steps going down on both sides. Both sides. Each side. And between the steps they had a bandstand that was high. Yeah.
It was the same was like the mother hall but you were good at going both sides. Yeah.
I saw I went there once at church. Jeannette you know. Yeah. Your sister-in-law took me there one time. 1943. But the bandstand wasn't there anymore then. It was all changed. You took it down.
